title: One-Syllable Clue · Classic
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play One-Syllable Clue · Classic with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: Write familiar objects on slips. The lead describes the chosen object using only one-syllable words without saying its name. The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule. Each player takes two turns. Give the lead one point for each successful turn. Highest score wins; ties are shared.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 2–8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In One-Syllable Clue, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The group identifies the object and the clue follows the word rule.
